chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, he said:
I asked him about a man who forgets the qunūt until he bows: should he perform qunūt? He said: No.

So it is possible that the meaning in these two reports is that making it up is not obligatory upon him; rather, it is only recommended, because initiating it is recommended, so how then would making it up be otherwise? And it is possible that what is meant by it is that he does not make it up when the circumstance is a circumstance of taqiyyah; that is indicated by this.

key_terms.الِابْتِدَاءَ: the initial performance of the act in its proper place
key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: making up an omitted act after its place has passed
key_terms.الْقُنُوتَ: the supplicatory act performed in salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: dissimulation for protection under constraining circumstances
key_terms.يَرْكَعَ: to enter rukuʿ, the bowing position in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets the qunūt until after entering rukuʿ in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of one who forgets the qunūt until reaching rukuʿ in salat (prayer), stating that he does not perform it at that point. The accompanying explanation indicates that making up the missed qunūt is not obligatory but recommended, and that in circumstances of taqiyyah it may be omitted altogether.
